name: Mount Paektu
blurb: Pine, larch and tundra on a volcano, where tigers, bears and nutcrackers share the slopes.

tip.title: Remove the Korean pine
tip.text: Pine seeds feed chipmunks, nutcrackers, wild boar and bears. Set Korean pine to -100% and watch the seed eaters first, then the tiger that hunts boar.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Long snowy winters
nodes.desc: The summit is cold and snowy for much of the year, and Heaven Lake is usually frozen from mid-October to mid-June.

nodes.name: Heaven Lake and meltwater
nodes.desc: The crater lake on the summit feeds the Songhua, Tumen and Yalu rivers, and its shores support a few hundred plant species.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Mount Paektu is a volcano, so its slopes are built on volcanic rock and ash that the forests and tundra grow in.

nodes.name: Soil fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen needles, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the volcanic soil.

nodes.name: Dahurian larch
nodes.desc: A cold-hardy conifer that, with mountain birch, grows on the upper forest slopes below the tundra.

nodes.name: Erman's birch
nodes.desc: A birch that forms the tree line on the mountain, growing where conifers thin out below the tundra.

nodes.name: Korean pine
nodes.desc: A large-seeded white pine of the old forests around Mount Paektu. Its seeds are carried off and buried by nutcrackers.

nodes.name: Alpine sedges and herbs
nodes.desc: Sedges and flowering herbs grow in the high meadows and tundra above the trees and feed grazers and seed eaters.

nodes.name: Stinging nettle
nodes.desc: A herb of moist, rich ground whose leaves feed the caterpillars of several butterflies.

nodes.name: Siberian chipmunk
nodes.desc: A ground-dwelling squirrel of northern forests that eats seeds and nuts and stores food for winter.

nodes.name: Korean pika
nodes.desc: A small rock-dwelling relative of rabbits found in the mountains of northern North Korea and the Changbai range.

nodes.name: Siberian roe deer
nodes.desc: A deer of forest and meadow that eats hundreds of plant species. Tigers, leopards and lynx all prey on it.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots in the forest floor for plants, seeds and small animals. A main prey of tigers in the Russian Far East.

nodes.name: Gray red-backed vole
nodes.desc: A small forest rodent that feeds on green plants and seeds and is prey for weasels and raptors.

nodes.name: Eurasian nutcracker
nodes.desc: A crow relative that caches pine seeds for winter. Forgotten caches help seed new trees.

nodes.name: Peacock butterfly
nodes.desc: A butterfly well recorded near the mountain. Its caterpillars feed on nettles.

nodes.name: Siberian weasel
nodes.desc: A small hunter of voles, hares and birds in forests and meadows.

nodes.name: Eurasian kestrel
nodes.desc: A small falcon that hunts voles and other small prey over open ground.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: An omnivorous crow, among the most recorded birds here, that also feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Gray wagtail
nodes.desc: A slim bird of mountain streams that catches insects, including butterflies.

nodes.name: Siberian tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator of the region's forests, hunting roe deer and wild boar. Numbers around Paektu are poorly known.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: A large omnivore of the region that eats pine seeds and often takes over tiger kills.
